Forcing: Ports & Junctions

Exogenous Forcing: A Changing Baseline Modified by Control

Source: vignettes/Forcing.Rmd
Forcing.Rmd

ramp.xds is designed for model building with progressive elaboration. To enable progressive elaboration, model object must include structures that can handle advanced set up options and functions to run the algorithms.
Most of these features will not be used most of the time, so they must be designed in and present for the software to work at all. In most cases, the features are turned off. This was handled by adding ports and junctions.

Ports

A port in ramp.xds or one of the satellite packages is an object that handles a term or parameter, such as temperature, other blood hosts, or search weights. Each port is defined by:

  • the port object

  • the value for the port and a function that returns it

  • advanced setup functions

  • an updating function

There are four classes of ports in SimBA.

  • Structural ports handle terms on an interface:

    • parameters or variables affecting the search for blood, blood feeding, transmission or exposure;

    • parameters or variables affecting the search for aquatic habitats and egg laying, and emergence;

  • Mosquito bionomics ports are designed to model malaria transmission by mosquitoes as a baseline that has been modified by control; these ports are handled by an MY module or an L module.

  • Epidemiology ports handle mass treatment; these ports are handled by an XH module

  • All other po

Ports — The design of a port and junction includes default setup of an object during xds_setup on the relevant object with parameter values set to have no effect; an advanced setup function setup_port that replaces the old default parameter, evaluates the port function and checks the returned value, and then rebuilds and replaces the port object; and a function update_port, called by a Junction, that evalutes the function and stores the updated value.

Junctions

A junction in ramp.xds is a function that implements several ports. The Junctions are called in xds_compute_terms, sandwiched between Interface Functions that set the values of terms that computed internally to handle transmission and exposure, or egg laying and emergence.

The order is designed to handle dependencies and minimize conflicts.

  • Forcing is a junction that handles weather, hydrology, shocks and development.

    • Weather \(\in\) ramp.forcing

      • temperature

      • rainfall

      • humidity

    • Hydrology \(\in\) ramp.forcing may depend on rainfall and temperature

      • water_level

      • water_temperature

    • Shock \(\in\) ramp.forcing

      • quarantine

      • conflict

    • Development \(\in\) ramp.forcing

      • gdp

      • housing

  • Health implements variables associated with health systems, which may depend on quarantine or conflict

    • nutrition

    • awareness

    • other_disease

  • Vector Control, part 1 (\(\in\) ramp.forcing) sets up variables associated with vector control, which may depend on weather variables.

  • Resources (\(\in\) ramp.forcing) handles ports associated with mosquito ecology that are not already part of one of the interfaces, which may depend on weather variables.

    • Availability of Sugar

    • Availability of Sugar Traps

  • Importation sets up the ports associated with malaria importation, which may depend on conflict or quarantine

    • time_away (\(\in\) XH_obj)

    • travel_eir (\(\in\) XH_obj)

    • visitors (\(\in\) patches)

    • vis_kappa (\(\in\) patches)

  • Blood Feeding handles all the ports that are part of the XY interface.

    • blood_search_weights (\(\in\) XH_obj)

    • time_spent (\(\in\) XH_obj)

    • other_blood_hosts (\(\in\) patches)

    • blood_traps (\(\in\) patches)

    • Compute Availability:

      • available_hosts — \(W\)

      • available_blood_hosts — \(B\)

  • Aquatic Habitats handles all the ports that are part of the MY interface.

    • habitat_search_weights (\(\in\) L_obj)

    • bad_habitats (\(\in\) patches)

    • ovitraps (\(\in\) patches)

    • Compute Availability:

      • available_habitats — \(Q\)

      • available_water — \(W\)

  • Mosquito Bionomics, part 1: a baseline — handles mosquito bionomics ports. Part 1 sets the value of a baseline as well as models for vector control that integrate the effects through resource availability.

    • MBionomics sets the value for adult mosquitoes (\(\in\) MY_obj)

    • LBionomics sets the value for immature mosquitoes (\(\in\) L_obj)

  • Vector Control, part 2 computes coverage and effect sizes of vector control, given the baseline.

  • Mosquito Bionomics, part 2: modified by control — handles effect sizes for mosquito bionomics ports

    • MEffectSizes applies effect sizes to bionomic parameters for adult mosquitoes (\(\in\) MY_obj)

    • LEffectSizes applies effect sizes to bionomic parameters for immature mosquitoes (\(\in\) L_obj)
